articles.title: Watch: What Americans think about the death penalty
articles.summary: The BBC spoke to Americans and international tourists in Washington DC about their views on the death penalty following the botched execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee.
articles.body:

articles.summary: Isaias will bring damaging winds, torrential rain and a storm surge with landfall expected late Friday.
articles.body:
Isaias, the first hurricane in the Atlantic this hurricane season has been continuing to strengthen and is now a category three 'major' hurricane.

Hurricane hunter aircraft have been flying in and around the storm on Friday morning, now measuring sustained wind speeds of 120mph (193km/h).

Isaias is expected to bring damaging winds, torrential rain and a storm surge to parts of the US Gulf Coast with landfall expected late Friday. Hurricane and storm surge watches have been issued.

It has been a record-breakingly quiet Atlantic season so far with development suppressed by the growing El Niño pattern.

articles.summary: Protests against sexual violence took place across more than 40 US states on 8 October.
articles.body:
Protests were held across the US on 8 October, calling for an end to sexual violence, following allegations of sexual assault involving members of a fraternity at Cornell University.

Survivors, students and advocates rallied and protested in communities and on college campuses across more than 40 states.

This comes after a lawsuit was filed against by “Jane Doe”, who alleges she was given drugs and alcohol before being sexually assaulted by several members of Cornell's Chi Phi fraternity while incapacitated in October 2024. She has accused Cornell University of failing to adequately investigate and discipline those involved.

Following the filing of the civil lawsuit, prosecutors reopened the case. New York Governor Kathy Hochul appointed the state’s attorney general as special prosecutor.

articles.title: Amazon’s Starlink competitor Leo gets a new date
articles.summary: Andy Jassy says the company’s space-internet service Leo (formerly known as Project Kuiper) will launch in mid-2026 as a rival to Starlink.
articles.body: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy says the company’s space-internet service Leo (formerly known as Project Kuiper) will “launch in mid-2026.” I’m going to assume that means proper commercial availability since the company already announced the start of an “enterprise preview” at the end of 2025, when the service was supposed to originally launch. Unlike SpaceX’s Starlink service, Amazon doesn’t (yet) have its own fleet of rockets to regularly send Leo satellites into low-Earth orbit. That’s meant hitching rides with a variety of launch partners, including SpaceX, until Jeff Bezos’ own reusable New Glenn rocket is fully operational. Amazon has FCC approval for 3,236 Leo satellites, but has only launched 241 so far, well below its commitment to have half (1,618) of its constellation deployed by July 2026. As such, Amazon has had to beg FCC Chair Brendan Carr for an extension. For comparison, SpaceX’s active Starlink constellation currently totals over 10,000 satellites. Whenever the Leo service does finally go live, Jassy says it will be faster than existing services and cost less, with the added benefit of integrating seamlessly with AWS so that businesses and governments can “move data back and forth for storage, analytics, and AI.” Late as it is, there are many individuals, enterprises, and nations just waiting on an Elon Musk alternative that can be installed quickly and economically to fill gaps in global data coverage, even if it does mean casting their lot with another problematic billionaire.

articles.title: NASA's hunting for a secret underground cave on the moon
articles.summary: Will future astronauts take shelter in moon caves?
articles.body:
When you buy through links on our articles, Future and its syndication partners may earn a commission.

Are there secret underground caves on the moon? NASA has a new program that aims to find out.

Though we see it in the sky most nights, the moon still holds an incredible amount of mystery. One such mystery is a large underground cave, or a cavernous tube carved out by ancient lava, that scientists think extends past a particular pit on the moon's surface. And to get to the bottom of it, NASA has selected a project known as GIMLI (the Geophysical Instruments for Marius Lunar pit Investigation, not the character from Lord of the Rings). GIMLI was selected along with two other programs that are all intended to expand our understanding of the moon to better support a future moon base, which NASA aims to build near the south pole.

"NASA Science is building the ultimate interplanetary survival guide to ensure that science goes first to the lunar surface to provide our future astronaut crews with the vital information, resources, and safety precautions needed ahead of time to survive the night on the moon," Nicky Fox, NASA's associate administrator for the Science Mission Directorate, said in a statement .

The site of this investigation will be the Marius Hill Pit, which was discovered in 2009 by Japan's Kaguya moon orbiter. You can see the pit clearly in the probe's images. But researchers think that there's more there than just a large hole in the lunar surface.

Theythink it's possible that the pit is connected to a vast, underground cave likely created by lava flowing in the ancient past. If true, this could shed light on the history of volcanic activity on the moon.

"Confirming a substantial lava tube would give us an insight into how volcanism operated on the moon," GIMLI deputy principal investigator Gareth Morgan said in a different statement. "Lava tubes are a common feature of basaltic volcanism on Earth, so identifying them on the moon means we could use knowledge of such terrestrial caves to better understand lunar history."

Even more, if researchers confirm the presence of this lava tube, astronauts could potentially use it as a natural shelter on the lunar surface. These lava-made caves would provide general shelter as well as protection from the extreme temperatures and radiation exposure experienced on the moon's surface. Lava tubes could also be a safe "bunker" of sorts where future astronauts could be shielded from micrometeorites. While a future moon base will probably have human-made shelters included, natural caves could be an incredible, existing resource that astronauts could tap into.

GIMLI will work directly on the lunar surface, scanning beneath to look for signs of the lava tube. This investigation comes from a proposal led by the nonprofit Planetary Science Institute (PSI) and will be funded through NASA's Payloads and Research Investigations on the Surface of the Moon (PRISM) program.

The investigation is partnering with Honeybee Robotics to help build the equipment and instrumentation that will be necessary for the study. This gear will get to the moon aboard a lander and rover via NASA's Commercial Lunar Payloads Services program, and the data collected will be studied by a team led by PSI associate director and senior scientist Than Putzig. The work done by PSI will be in partnership with the Norwegian Space Agency.

From the lunar surface, GIMLI will gather data using ground-penetrating radar, seismic sensors and a gravimeter to better understand what's really happening underneath the surface. These measurements will allow GIMLI to determine if there is a subsurface lava tube and, if so, how big it is. Could it fit an entire astronaut crew? We will have to wait and see.

articles.title: Trump gives top US science awards to Elon Musk and other tech executives
articles.summary: The National Medal of Science is annually given to scientists and engineers for major contributions in their fields.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump has awarded the country’s most prestigious honours in science and engineering to executives from top technology firms including SpaceX, Alphabet, Microsoft and Nvidia.

On Thursday, Trump presented the National Medal of Science to billionaire SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Google co-founder Sergey Brin, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Lisa Su of the semiconductor firm AMD.

Two more recipients received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation: Michael Dell of Dell Technologies and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella.

At the award ceremony, Trump credited the honourees with “helping pioneer an incredible future for America”.

“Because of these people here, we will always be on top. No one else can compete with us,” Trump said.

Five of the six people receiving medals on Thursday were born outside the US. Four are among the 10 wealthiest people in the world, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

The award ceremony took place hours after the Trump administration announced it was suspending Microsoft and other top tech companies from using the H-1B visa system, which allows companies to hire skilled foreign workers and put them on a path towards permanent residency in the US.

The suspension, officials said, was due to the companies allegedly using the system in a fraudulent manner.

White House builds ties with Silicon Valley

The medal ceremony was the latest example of what critics see as an increasingly close relationship between Silicon Valley tech executives and the second Trump administration.

Powerful companies like Amazon, Meta and Nvidia contributed money to Trump’s second inauguration, and several high-profile industry leaders attended his swearing-in, including Musk and Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.

Trump, for his part, has pledged to slash regulations and position the US “as the world leader in artificial intelligence”.

He has also touted self-regulation in the AI industry amid concerns about the safety of the technology.

Several of the tech entrepreneurs honoured on Thursday have forged close ties to the White House, through political and business dealings.

The South Africa-born Musk, for example, was the largest contributor to Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign and has been a supporter of right-wing causes around the world, which he amplifies on his social media platform, X.

He briefly served as a special adviser to the president during the first months of Trump’s second term, helping to lead the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) and its efforts to downsize the federal government.

Around the time he left DOGE, however, Musk and Trump had a public falling-out over the president’s tax-and-spending plans.

The two have since reconciled. On Thursday, Trump hailed Musk as “our modern-day Thomas Edison” and an “industrial titan”, citing his work with the aerospace company SpaceX and the carmaker Tesla.

“Few Americans in history have done more to advance America’s national interest than Elon in one field after another,” Trump said.

Another honouree, Dell, has been a financial backer of the president’s efforts to launch Trump Accounts, a scheme to enrol American children born during Trump’s second term into government-backed investment accounts.

Dell and his wife Susan Dell committed $6.25bn to the programme last year.

Separately, the White House entered into a deal in August for the US government to take a 15 percent cut of any AI chip sales that Nvidia and AMD make with China.

Huang, Nvidia’s co-founder, later invested in the struggling US tech firm Intel. He is reported to be among the donors financing Trump’s plans for a new White House ballroom.

The National Medal of Science was first awarded in 1963 to Theodore von Karman, a pioneer in aerospace engineering who fled anti-Semitism in Europe during World War II.

He went on to help found the Jet Propulsion Laboratory at the California Institute of Technology.

Nominations for the award are solicited by the National Science Foundation, and the recipients are ultimately selected by a committee appointed by the president.

articles.title: SpaceX announces plan to become a ‘major mobile carrier’
articles.summary: SpaceX is acquiring a portfolio of low-band spectrum that the company says will “pave the way” for Starlink Mobile to become a major US carrier.
articles.body: SpaceX has acquired a portfolio of low-band spectrum licenses — a move the company says “will pave the way” for its Starlink Mobile service to become a “major” US carrier. When the Federal Communications Commission signs off on the deal, SpaceX says it will deploy its new architecture that combines its satellite-to-mobile constellation with a terrestrial mobile network, directly competing with T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon. The licenses include up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz band, which SpaceX says will allow Starlink Mobile’s signal to penetrate through walls and buildings. SpaceX previously acquired 2GHz spectrum from EchoStar as part of efforts to bolster its direct-to-device service. The FCC has also approved plans to deploy 15,000 V2 Starlink Mobile satellites that will offer more than 100 times the bandwidth than the current generation, according to SpaceX. “With this new low-band spectrum and our Gen2 constellation, Starlink Mobile can now become the first network operator to deploy both satellite and terrestrial spectrum,” SpaceX says. “One network that provides Americans with a reliable service indoors, outdoors, in cellular dead zones, and everywhere in between.”

articles.title: Scientists identified a new extinct crocodile species from the same Egyptian rocks used to build the Great Sphinx; even the fossil is missing the tip of its snout, echoing the monument
articles.summary: Long before the Great Sphinx became one of Egypt’s most recognisable monuments, the landscape around Cairo was home to a very different kind of
articles.body: Long before the Great Sphinx became one of Egypt’s most recognisable monuments, the landscape around Cairo was home to a very different kind of long-snouted creature. Now, a fossil discovered from the same ancient rocks used to construct the Sphinx has revealed a new species of extinct crocodile and it comes with an extraordinary coincidence. The fossil is missing the tip of its snout, creating an uncanny parallel with the monument’s famously absent nose. The species, named Herugavialis cairensis, has been identified through a fresh examination of fossils recovered nearly a century ago. The findings, published in Royal Society Open Science, offer a glimpse into a time when crocodiles thrived in the ancient Mediterranean.A crocodile lost to timeAccording to a report published by Phys Org, the fossils were originally recovered during the 1920s from Egypt’s roughly 45-million-year-old Mokattam Formation. Among them was a remarkably well-preserved skull that had been classified as belonging to Tomistoma, the group commonly associated with the modern false gharial. That identification, however, was based largely on the fossil’s outward resemblance to the living species. Modern paleontological techniques have now allowed researchers to take a much closer look.CT scanning, in particular, enabled scientists to examine the internal structure of the skull without damaging the fossil. Combined with new analytical methods, the investigation revealed a series of anatomical differences significant enough to establish the crocodile as a previously unrecognised species, adds the report.The skull of Herugavialis cairensis remains relatively complete, although its missing snout tip became one of the most intriguing details of the discovery, claims the findings.The gharial connectionAccording to the findings, gavials are distinguished by their unusually long, slender snouts, a feature adapted to their specialised feeding habits. Today, only two living species remain: the critically endangered gharial, Gavialis gangeticus, found on the Indian subcontinent, and Tomistoma schlegelii, the false gharial of Southeast Asia.Their evolutionary history, however, is considerably more expansive. Fossil gavials have been found across much of the world and represent a lineage that stretches back more than 100 million years. Unlike their modern descendants, many ancient species inhabited shallow marine environments, adds the findings. Also, Herugavialis adds another piece to this complex evolutionary story, showing that ancient Egypt once supported a surprisingly rich assemblage of long-snouted crocodilians.Egypt’s ancient crocodile coastAs per Phys Org, around 45 million years ago, the landscape of what is now Egypt looked dramatically different. Shallow marine environments covered parts of the region, creating habitats capable of supporting several crocodile species.Herugavialis was far from alone. At least two other gavial species inhabited the region during the same broad period, pointing to a Mediterranean ecosystem with considerably greater crocodile diversity than exists today.The findings suggest that diversity appears to have shifted alongside major changes in Earth's climate and sea levels. Over millions of years, the Mediterranean environment underwent profound transformations, eventually becoming inhospitable to crocodilians.A strange echo of the SphinxAccording to Royal Society Open Science, the discovery carries an almost poetic connection to one of Egypt's most famous monuments. The Mokattam rocks that preserved the fossil also contributed to the geological material from which the Great Sphinx was carved. Even more striking is the missing anatomy, as the Sphinx is renowned for its damaged and absent nose, while the fossil crocodile is missing the end of its own snout. The coincidence inspired the name Herugavialis, drawing on Heru, the ancient Egyptian deity associated with the falcon-headed god Horus and thought by the researchers to have potentially influenced the imagery of the Sphinx, the findings conclude.Image Courtesy: Phys Org

articles.title: Ilê Aiyê abre inscrições para concurso Deusa do Ébano 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Mulheres negras de todo o Brasil, com idades entre 18 e 35 anos, podem se candidatar. Inscrições vão até 5 de dezembro e as finalistas serão anunciadas no dia 12.
articles.summary: Mulheres negras de todo o Brasil, com idades entre 18 e 35 anos, podem se candidatar. Inscrições vão até 5 de dezembro e as finalistas serão anunciadas no dia 12.
articles.body:
Ilê Aiyê abre inscrições para concurso 'Deusa do Ébano' 2027 — Foto: André Frutuôso/Estúdio Casa de Mainha

O bloco afro Ilê Aiyê abre, neste sábado (10), as inscrições para o concurso Deusa do Ébano 2027. Mulheres negras de todo o Brasil, com idades entre 18 e 35 anos podem se candidatar. As inscrições vão até o dia 5 de dezembro.

De acordo com a organização do concurso, é importante que as participantes conheçam a história do bloco afro. Durante o processo de inscrição, as candidatas deverão preencher um formulário, disponível no site do Ilê Aiyê e anexar fotos em trajes que não sejam de banho ou roupas íntimas.

A primeira etapa do concurso está prevista para 12 de dezembro, quando serão anunciadas as 15 finalistas que permanecerão na disputa pelo título de Rainha do Ilê Aiyê.

A vencedora do concurso será anunciada durante a 46ª edição do evento Noite da Beleza Negra. Neste momento, as finalistas subirão ao palco para disputar a coroa de Deusa do Ébano. As candidaturas devem ser realizadas por meio do site do Ilê.

A iniciativa pretende celebrar a identidade negra e a trajetória das mulheres negras. O Ilê Aiyê realiza o concurso Deusa do Ébano desde 1976, quando aconteceu a primeira Noite da Beleza Negra.

Atualmente, a Deusa do Ébano é Carol Xavier, estudante de Jornalismo, empreendedora, dançarina, atriz e professora de dança afro infantil. Moradora da comunidade de Sussuarana, em Salvador , ela conquistou o título em 2026, após ter sido eleita princesa do concurso em 2024.

articles.title: Fortuna de Elon Musk: simulador permite gastar US$ 1 trilhão | G1
articles.standfirst: Criado pela revista norte-americana Wired, site gratuito permite comprar até 200 estádios de futebol americano ou quase 12 mil jatinhos particulares. E ainda sobra dinheiro.
articles.summary: A fortuna de Elon Musk pode comprar 200 estádios ou 12 mil jatinhos em novo simulador gratuito criado pela revista Wired para ilustrar o valor de US$ 1 trilhão.
articles.body:
Simulador permite gastar US$ 1 trilhão da fortuna de Elon Musk — Foto: Reprodução/Wired

Um site permite ter um gostinho de como seria ser Elon Musk e gastar US$ 1 trilhão (cerca de R$ 5 trilhões, na conversão) de sua fortuna.

Nele, é possível torrar toda essa grana comprando desde cafés, Big Macs e iPhones até ônibus escolares, Lamborghinis, carros de Fórmula 1, satélites, navios e estádios de futebol. Também é possível gastar dinheiro com advogados e tanques de guerra, entre outros itens.

O simulador é gratuito e foi desenvolvido pela revista norte-americana de tecnologia Wired em parceria com o site de jogos Neal.fun ( acesse aqui ).

Em junho deste ano, Elon Musk se tornou o primeiro trilionário da história após a estreia da SpaceX na Nasdaq, principal bolsa de tecnologia dos Estados Unidos, que reúne empresas como Apple, Google e Microsoft.

Nascido na África do Sul, Musk é hoje a pessoa mais rica do mundo e construiu sua fortuna com empresas como Tesla, SpaceX, Starlink e X , o antigo Twitter.

Segundo a revista Wired, pesquisas mostram que as pessoas têm dificuldade para compreender números tão altos. Por isso, o simulador busca ajudar o público a ter uma ideia do que significa possuir uma fortuna de US$ 1 trilhão.

"Talvez uma maneira melhor de visualizar um trilhão de dólares seja por meio do que você realmente pode comprar com ele", afirma a revista.

Nos testes do g1 , foi possível comprar 833 mil iPhones, por US$ 1.200 cada, e gastar cerca de US$ 1 bilhão da fortuna de Musk.

US$ 1 tri: simulador permite gastar toda a fortuna de Musk com hambúrgueres, cavalos, mansões e mais — Foto: Reprodução/Wired

Em outra simulação, deu para comprar 200 estádios da NFL, liga de futebol americano dos Estados Unidos, por US$ 5 bilhões cada. Nesse caso, toda a fortuna foi consumida.

Outra opção foi comprar quase 12 mil jatinhos particulares, por US$ 85 milhões cada. Mesmo depois de gastar tanto dinheiro, ainda sobrariam cerca de US$ 60 bilhões para comprar outros itens disponíveis no simulador.

Elon Musk, dono da Tesla e da SpaceX, durante cerimônia de posse em Washington, DC, em 20 de janeiro de 2025. — Foto: SAUL LOEB/Pool via REUTERS

articles.title: Marte na Terra? Lago na Turquia tem águas 'de outro mundo' | G1
articles.standfirst: O lago Salda, na Turquia, parece as Maldivas, mas seus minerais são iguais aos de um antigo lago em Marte.
articles.summary: O lago Salda, na Turquia, parece as Maldivas, mas seus minerais são iguais aos de um antigo lago em Marte.
articles.body:
O lago Salda é famoso por suas águas azul-turquesa e suas praias de areia branca.

Sua margem é rica em hidromagnesita, um mineral claro que dá ao lugar esse visual tropical.

Mas a história não para por aí: o lago Salda é praticamente uma ponte entre mundos!

Isso porque ele é o equivalente natural mais próximo, na Terra, da Cratera Jezero, em Marte, onde o rover Perseverance da Nasa pousou em 2021.

Bem, os cientistas acreditam que Jezero também já foi um lago.

Uma ilustração mostra a Cratera Jezero, como ela teria sido há bilhões de anos atrás, se tivesse sido um lago — Foto: NASA/JPL-CALTECH

Isso porque sua antiga linha costeira e suas formações semelhantes a deltas são surpreendentemente parecidas com as encontradas em Salda.

E fica ainda mais interessante: tanto Salda quanto Jezero contêm o mesmo tipo de carbonatos ricos em magnésio.

Além disso, Salda possui estruturas parecidas com rochas, construídas por microrganismos, chamadas microbialitos.

Os cientistas se interessam por elas porque estruturas semelhantes em Marte podem ser nossa melhor chance de encontrar vestígios de vida passada, caso ela tenha existido em Jezero.

Rover Perseverance trabalha em torno de um afloramento rochoso chamado "Skinner Ridge", na cratera Jezero de Marte. — Foto: Nasa/Divulgação

É por isso que cientistas da Nasa estudaram esse lago turco antes mesmo de o rover chegar a Marte.

Então, sim: a beleza de Salda é literalmente de outro mundo!

articles.title: Quase todo mundo vira naturalmente para a esquerda ao caminhar | G1
articles.standfirst: Independentemente da idade, do gênero, da cultura e das circunstâncias, as multidões sempre caminham em uma espiral no sentido anti-horário
articles.summary: Independentemente da idade, do gênero, da cultura e das circunstâncias, as multidões sempre caminham em uma espiral no sentido anti-horário
articles.body:
Essa história começou, como tantas outras na história da ciência, com algo que não estávamos procurando.

Em 2020, durante a pandemia da COVID-19, estávamos estudando uma questão prática: como as pessoas se movimentam em um espaço fechado quando se pede que mantenham distância umas das outras?

Assistindo às imagens repetidas vezes, percebemos algo estranho: quase todos os participantes andavam em círculos que giravam na mesma direção, sempre no sentido anti-horário . Mais estranho ainda, nenhum deles parecia ter percebido que estava fazendo isso.

Essa observação nos levou a uma jornada de cinco anos para descobrir por que os seres humanos se comportam dessa maneira.

O efeito em si é fácil de descrever. Deixe uma multidão circular dentro de um espaço fechado sem destino específico, e ela lentamente começa a girar, quase sempre para a esquerda. Ninguém dirige esse movimento. Ninguém decide isso.

Para um físico, isso parece um exemplo clássico de “comportamento emergente”: um padrão coletivo que surge de inúmeras pequenas interações, seja entre indivíduos, seja entre indivíduos e o ambiente ao seu redor. Essas foram nossas duas hipóteses principais, que tentamos validar isoladamente.

Nossa primeira suspeita girava em torno da interação entre os pedestres e as paredes da sala. Um estudo anterior de neurociência havia constatado que pessoas destras tendem a virar para a esquerda e as canhotas, para a direita — um viés sutil ligado a pequenas diferenças entre as duas metades do cérebro.

Como a maioria do nosso grupo original era destra, era razoável supor que o movimento coletivo em espiral não passava da soma das preferências individuais, transformada em um círculo pelas paredes que os cercavam.

Para testar isso, elaboramos um novo experimento que começou antes mesmo de a multidão se reunir na arena. Um voluntário por vez caminhava em linha reta em direção a uma parede, e registrávamos para que lado ele virava ao chegar lá.

Sabendo a preferência de cada um, pudemos então classificar as pessoas por essa característica e observar o resultado.

Se as paredes e a lateralidade fossem a resposta, um grupo de canhotos ou, melhor ainda, de pessoas que virassem exclusivamente para a direita, acabaria por inverter a rotação e se mover no sentido horário. Isso nunca aconteceu.

Quer enchêssemos a sala com pessoas que viravam para a direita ou com canhotos, a tendência de girar no sentido anti-horário se manteve.

Talvez a presença das paredes, por si só, estivesse por trás desse efeito de orientação. Para descobrir, levamos o experimento para o ar livre, em um pátio escolar aberto muito grande, de 3.000 metros quadrados, sem paredes de delimitação, e deixamos mais de cem adolescentes caminharem sem nada para guiá-los.

O efeito de rotação não apenas persistiu, como se intensificou. A sala, evidentemente, não era a responsável.

Isso nos deixou com nosso segundo suspeito: a maneira como interagimos uns com os outros. Quando dois pedestres se encontram de frente, cada um se desvia para o lado, levando ao conhecido fenômeno da formação de faixas.

Mas o lado que escolhemos não é aleatório e geralmente é determinado pelo lado da via em que as pessoas dirigem. Na Espanha, assim como no resto da Europa continental - e no Brasil -, nos desviamos para a direita, o que deixa algum espaço à nossa esquerda para que a pessoa que se aproxima faça o mesmo.

Talvez, raciocinamos, a origem do movimento no sentido anti-horário não fosse nada além de uma manifestação desse fenômeno. Se os pedestres tendem a se deslocar para a direita a cada interação, eles acabarão caminhando com a parede à direita, movendo-se no sentido anti-horário.

Se isso fosse verdade, uma multidão japonesa deveria girar no sentido horário porque, no Japão, as pessoas dirigem e se deslocam para a esquerda, e a formação de faixas ocorre no lado oposto ao nosso.

Entramos em contato com um colega em Tóquio, convencidos de que ele observaria a multidão girar no sentido horário. Novos experimentos resultaram em um novo fracasso . A multidão japonesa girou no sentido anti-horário, portanto, nossa hipótese estava errada.

Uma explicação cultural ainda permanecia: um hábito adquirido em algum momento da vida, como a direção anti-horária na qual quase todas as pistas de atletismo são construídas. Então, recorremos a crianças da pré-escola, que mal começaram a absorver as convenções dos adultos. Longe de desaparecer, a tendência delas no sentido anti-horário foi a mais forte que medimos em qualquer lugar.

Se não é o grupo, o ambiente ou nossos hábitos sociais, restava apenas um lugar: uma característica puramente individual, algo biomecânico ou arraigado no cérebro .

Para testar isso, pedimos a mais de 200 voluntários que caminhassem sozinhos, um de cada vez, em uma arena vazia. Sem ninguém com quem colidir e sem multidão para seguir, uma clara maioria ainda se movia no sentido anti-horário.

Por décadas, nossa área de estudo partiu do princípio de que padrões coletivos como esse emergem das interações entre pedestres. Neste caso, os dados mostram exatamente o oposto: o padrão já está presente em uma única pessoa caminhando sozinha.

De fato, ao inserir apenas esses dados de movimento individual em um modelo, conseguimos reproduzir o redemoinho de toda a multidão. Nesse caso, e ao contrário do que ocorre em fenômenos coletivos emergentes, o todo não é maior do que a soma das partes; é exatamente o mesmo.

E aqui está a conclusão sincera: ainda não sabemos a causa desse viés no nível individual. Procuramos uma relação com a lateralidade (mão dominante), o pé dominante, o olho dominante, o sexo, etc e não encontramos nada.

Estudos com pessoas caminhando com os olhos vendados, que tendem a se desviar em espiral para um lado, sugerem algo mais profundo, talvez assimetrias sutis no ouvido interno que alteram minimamente nossa percepção de linha reta. Mas, no momento, não podemos oferecer nenhuma explicação para isso.

De qualquer forma, saber que essa tendência é individual e não coletiva ainda é valioso e pode mudar a forma como modelamos e projetamos os espaços que compartilhamos: lugares como aeroportos, estações de trem e museus, onde o fluxo harmonioso de pessoas é importante.

Essa mesma inclinação para a esquerda aparece até mesmo em animais, por exemplo, em cardumes de peixes e nas colônias em espiral das formigas-correição. A força que empurra um ser humano sozinho para a esquerda pode, no fim das contas, acabar sendo muito mais antiga do que a própria Humanidade.

*Iñaki Echeverría Huarte é professor assistente na Universidade de Navarra.

*Angel Garcimartín Montero é professor de Física da Matéria Condensada na Universidade de Navarra.

*Iker Zuriguel Ballaz é professor de Física Aplicada na Universidade de Navarra.

**Este texto foi publicado originalmente no site do The Conversation Brasil.

articles.title: Por que cães grandes envelhecem mais rápido e têm uma vida mais curta? | G1
articles.standfirst: Estudo com 864 cães encontrou mudanças no DNA associadas ao envelhecimento mais acelerado em raças maiores. Pesquisadores dizem que mecanismo ainda precisa ser melhor entendido.
articles.summary: Estudo com 864 cães encontrou mudanças no DNA ligadas ao envelhecimento mais acelerado em animais maiores, mas ainda não prova que elas sejam a causa.
articles.body:
Cães de diferentes portes caminham juntos; estudo investigou por que animais maiores tendem a envelhecer mais rápido e viver menos. — Foto: Pexels

Cães de raças grandes costumam envelhecer mais rápido e viver menos do que os pequenos.

Um novo estudo publicado na revista "Science" encontrou uma possível explicação para essa diferença.

Pesquisadores analisaram o DNA de 864 cães que fazem parte do "Dog Aging Project", um grande projeto de pesquisa sobre envelhecimento canino, e identificaram mudanças que acontecem com a idade e aparecem de forma mais acentuada nos animais de maior porte.

O foco do trabalho foram trechos do DNA conhecidos como “ genes saltadores ”, capazes de se copiar e ocupar novas posições no material genético.

Esses trechos normalmente ficam sob controle de marcas químicas que ajudam a manter sua atividade regulada. Com o passar do tempo, parte desse controle se perde.

Segundo o estudo, essa perda foi especialmente forte em regiões ligadas a um tipo desses genes, chamado LINE1 .

Nas raças gigantes, a redução dessas marcas aconteceu, em média, 35% mais rápido por ano do que nas raças pequenas.

Os pesquisadores dizem que isso pode ajudar a explicar por que cães maiores envelhecem mais depressa e também têm maior risco de doenças ligadas à idade.

“Embora saibamos que os cães de grande porte vivem menos do que os cães menores, ainda não sabemos exatamente por quê”, afirmou ao g1 Noah Snyder-Mackler, autor sênior do estudo e professor da Universidade do Estado do Arizona.

"Este estudo apresenta uma possível explicação: alterações relacionadas ao envelhecimento na metilação do DNA, um processo químico que regula a atividade dos genes, ocorrem mais rapidamente no sistema imunológico desses animais".

Os cientistas analisaram um processo chamado metilação do DNA, que funciona como uma espécie de controle sobre a atividade dos genes, sem alterar a sequência do DNA.

Cães de portes diferentes caminham lado a lado. — Foto: Pexels

Esse controle muda com a idade. No estudo, mais de 40% das regiões associadas ao LINE1 perderam metilação ao longo do envelhecimento, o que fez desse grupo um dos mais afetados.

Quando esse controle diminui, os “genes saltadores” podem ficar mais ativos e provocar alterações no DNA. Esse processo já foi associado, em outros estudos, ao envelhecimento, ao câncer e a outras doenças.

Os autores, porém, fazem uma ressalva: ainda não é possível dizer se essa mudança causa o envelhecimento mais rápido ou se acontece como consequência dele.

A diferença entre cães grandes e pequenos chama atenção porque, entre espécies diferentes, o padrão costuma ser o contrário: animais maiores geralmente vivem mais .

Baleias, por exemplo, podem viver muito mais do que pequenos mamíferos.

Nos cães, dentro da mesma espécie, os maiores tendem a crescer mais rápido, envelhecer antes e viver menos. É essa diferença que o novo estudo tenta explicar.

O trabalho também encontrou diferenças entre machos e fêmeas em regiões do cromossomo X , mas os pesquisadores dizem que ainda é cedo para saber quanto isso influencia o envelhecimento.

Segundo os autores, entender melhor esses mecanismos pode ajudar a estudar não só a longevidade dos cães, mas também processos semelhantes em outros mamíferos.

"Essa descoberta é relevante não apenas para os cães, mas também para a nossa compreensão do envelhecimento em seres humanos e outros animais. Isso porque grande parte do que encontramos pode se aplicar à maioria dos mamíferos, devido às semelhanças em nosso código genético", acrescentou Snyder-Mackler.

articles.title: Rumbling volcano forces immediate trail closures at popular vacation hot spot
articles.summary: The Kīlauea volcano shows renewed spattering at two vents as USGS scientists monitor for a possible 55th episode of lava fountains at the summit.
articles.body: Officials are monitoring renewed volcanic activity at one of Hawaii's most popular tourist destinations as hundreds of earthquakes and rockfall risks prompt temporary trail closures. The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) issued a volcanic activity notice earlier this week for the Kīlauea volcano at Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park, reporting renewed spattering at two vents following recent activity beneath the summit. The National Park Service (NPS) announced Wednesday that Halemaʻumaʻu Trail and part of Byron Ledge Trail would temporarily close amid increased seismic activity and concerns about rockfalls. The closures affect a combined 1.3 miles of trails. HUSBAND AND WIFE GET TRAPPED IN PREMIER HIKING DESTINATION; ONLY ONE OF THEM MAKES IT OUT ALIVE Over 200 shallow earthquakes were recorded beneath Kīlauea's summit during the past week, according to the NPS, citing the Hawaiian Volcano Observatory. A magnitude-3.4 earthquake on Sept. 30 caused small rockfalls along the caldera's north wall. Kīlauea remained at an ORANGE aviation color code, the second-highest level on the USGS' four-tier scale, as of Thursday. The designation indicates heightened volcanic activity and the potential for an eruption, or an eruption underway with limited hazards to aviation. The intrusion, which occurred from Sept. 30 to Oct. 1, is believed to have caused new cracks along the caldera floor, according to scientists. Scientists said they cannot forecast when — or if — the volcano's 55th episode of lava fountaining will occur. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "Forecast windows for episode 55 fountaining can no longer be modeled due to changes in conditions," the USGS advisory said. Officials also outlined several hazards for residents and visitors, including potentially dangerous gas emissions and small, glassy volcanic fragments that can cause skin and eye irritation. "Small glassy volcanic fragments may be remobilized during windy conditions following recent eruptive episodes," the statement added. "Residents and visitors should minimize exposure to these fragments, which can cause skin and eye irritation." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Visitors must also stay out of closed areas and away from unstable cliff edges, which can collapse without warning, according to the NPS. Kīlauea, one of the world's most active volcanoes, has erupted dozens of times since 1952, according to the USGS. Eruptive activity was nearly continuous along the volcano's East Rift Zone from 1983 to 2018, a 35-year stretch that ended amid significant eruptive activity and a collapse at the summit, the agency said. Since December 2024, an eruption has been intermittently active within Halema'uma'u crater at the summit. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The National Park Service has said the number of visits surged during Kīlauea's eruptive episodes, with tourists drawn to opportunities to view the volcanic activity. Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park recorded more than 1.8 million recreational visits in 2025, according to NPS data. articles.title: Once near extinction, these giant tortoises now outnumber people in the Seychelles, survey finds
articles.summary: Giant tortoises once pushed to the brink of extinction now outnumber humans in their home of the Seychelles, according to a new survey on one of the African...
articles.body:
Giant tortoises once pushed to the brink of extinction now outnumber humans in their home of the Seychelles, according to a new survey on one of the African nation's most remote islands.

The survey , led by the Seychelles Islands Foundation (SIF) and the University of Exeter in the UK, estimated that about 180,000 Aldabra giant tortoises live on Aldabra Atoll, an Indian Ocean island group off the east coast of mainland Africa.

It is the highest figure ever recorded for the species, and far exceeds the human population of around 122,000 living in the tiny archipelago nation.

Aldabra Atoll is one of only two places in the world where giant tortoises are found in the wild. A much smaller population lives on Ecuador's Galápagos Islands.

One of the world's most undisturbed island ecosystems, Aldabra Atoll is home to several unique species that thrive in the remote haven.

The species has rebounded from a dramatic decline. Heavy exploitation during the 19th century reduced its population on the island to fewer than 1,000, pushing the species to the brink of extinction.

A recovery program helped secure strict nature reserve status for the atoll in 1981. It became a UNESCO World Heritage site a year later, giving the population room to rebound.

"More than 180,000 giant tortoises roaming freely on our atoll is proof of what long-term commitment to conservation can achieve," Frauke Fleischer-Dogley, CEO of SIF, said in a statement.

"This is wonderful news for Seychelles, for the world, and for everyone who has worked to protect Aldabra."

Creating the new estimate required more than just a headcount. The figures are based on an analysis of five years of tortoise counts conducted between 2018 and 2022, and is the first update since a widely cited estimate of 100,000 tortoises in the late 1990s.

"Aldabra's giant tortoise monitoring program is one of the longest running in the region, but the atoll's dense vegetation makes counting tortoises genuinely difficult in places," said Nancy Bunbury, one of the study's co-authors.

Bunbury added the team of scientists on the study have produced the most reliable baseline for the species, which can be used as a benchmark to track its population for decades to come.

Despite the encouraging population estimate, the study's authors said continued vigilance is crucial as the climate crisis brings longer and more frequent droughts that could reduce shade and food for the tortoises. Rising sea levels as the planet warms also threaten the atoll's low-lying habitat.

The world's oldest known tortoise, a 194-year-old called Jonathan , is likely to have come from the Aldabra Atoll or the Granitic Seychelles.

Guinness World Records lists Jonathan as the oldest living land animal and the oldest tortoise ever. He was believed to be about 50 years old when he was moved to the British Overseas Territory of St. Helena in 1882.

articles.title: Billionaire Donald Bren led the permanent protection of more than 57,500 acres of California’s historic Irvine Ranch, nearly 60% of the property; almost 40,000 acres later received National Natural Landmark status
articles.summary: Billionaire real-estate developer Donald Bren helped turn a significant portion of California’s historic Irvine Ranch into a vast network of protected
articles.body: Billionaire real-estate developer Donald Bren helped turn a significant portion of California’s historic Irvine Ranch into a vast network of protected public lands, with 57,500 acres now preserved as open space and parklands. The scale of the conservation effort has been documented by the Irvine Ranch Conservancy, the City of Irvine and the National Park Service, while historical reporting by the Los Angeles Times traces the federal landmark designation and the later expansion of protected land. The protected acreage represents roughly 60% of the original 93,000-acre Irvine Ranch, a sprawling property that extends across parts of Orange County from the Santa Ana Mountains toward the Pacific coast. Rather than remaining a privately controlled expanse, much of the land was transferred to public agencies to be preserved for recreation, wildlife and conservation.The transformation unfolded over decades. Bren became chairman of the Irvine Company in 1983 and subsequently played a central role in shaping how the ranch would develop. Major conservation milestones followed, including an 11,000-acre open-space gift announced in 2001 and the transfer of roughly 20,000 acres to Orange County in 2010. In 2014, another 2,500 acres was added, bringing the permanently preserved total to more than 57,000 acres.The landscape is significant not simply because of its size. In 2006, about 37,000 acres of the Irvine Ranch received National Natural Landmark status from the U.S. Department of the Interior following scientific evaluation coordinated through the National Park Service. Researchers identified unusually valuable geological formations as well as rare and threatened habitats. The area contains coastal sage scrub and chaparral communities and provides habitat for species including the California gnatcatcher, peregrine falcon and Pacific pocket mouse.Two years later, the same landscape received California Natural Landmark recognition, making the Irvine Ranch notable for its combined federal and state landmark designations. The National Park Service continues to list Irvine Ranch among the National Natural Landmarks designated in 2006.Protecting the land was only the beginning. In 2005, the Irvine Ranch Conservancy was established as a nonprofit organisation to help public landowners care for the protected landscapes while maintaining responsible public access. The Irvine Company and Bren provided initial financial support as part of a broader $50 million commitment toward conservation and public enjoyment.Over the past two decades, the conservancy has expanded its role beyond simply maintaining trails. Its work includes habitat restoration, invasive-species removal, scientific monitoring, wildfire prevention and volunteer programmes. The organisation says it has restored more than 2,000 acres of native habitat and built and maintained hundreds of miles of trails since its founding.The conservation story also illustrates how a heavily developed region can retain substantial stretches of wilderness. These protected lands support diverse wildlife, provide recreational opportunities for local communities, preserve important ecosystems, and help maintain ecological connections across the region.Today, the Irvine Ranch’s protected areas include oak-filled canyons, coastal habitats, foothills and rugged terrain, creating a connected landscape unusually close to major urban communities. What began as a historic ranch has therefore become something considerably larger: an urban conservation network where land once vulnerable to development is now intended to remain open for future generations.

articles.title: Norway turned 20 tonnes of aluminium from a decommissioned oil platform into a 55-metre pedestrian bridge
articles.summary: Norway has given old oil-industry material a very different purpose, turning 20 tonnes of aluminium recovered from the decommissioned Gyda oil platform
articles.body: Norway has given old oil-industry material a very different purpose, turning 20 tonnes of aluminium recovered from the decommissioned Gyda oil platform into part of a new pedestrian and cycle bridge in Trondheim. The 55-metre Hangarbrua crosses the railway at Leangen Station and is the first aluminium bridge built in Norway since 1995. Its deck is made entirely from recycled aluminium, creating a project that links the country’s offshore industrial past with a new piece of urban infrastructure. The bridge also serves as a test project for future aluminium construction.How did 20 tonnes of oil platform aluminium become a 55-metre bridgeThe story begins with Gyda, a North Sea oil platform that operated from 1990 until it was decommissioned in 2021. Aker Solutions dismantled the platform, recovering 18,000 tonnes of steel and other metals, including aluminium from its topsides. Stena Recycling sorted the recovered aluminium before selling the scrap to Hydro for recycling.Hydro then processed the aluminium at its facilities in Sweden. The company cast the recovered material into extrusion ingots at its Sjunnen casthouse before transporting it to its extrusion plant in Finspang. There, it was turned into new aluminium profiles that could be used for the bridge deck. The process allowed material that had once been part of offshore infrastructure to become part of a public structure in Trondheim.The Norwegian Public Roads Administration commissioned Hangarbrua as a pilot project. Leirvik AS designed and built the bridge with COWI, while Hydro, Aker Solutions and Stena worked together on the recycled aluminium deck. The project brought together companies with experience in offshore structures, recycling and bridge design.What makes the Hangarbrua different from a conventional bridgeHangarbrua is 55 metres long and 9 metres wide, with a total weight of 60 tonnes. It is a network arch bridge designed for pedestrians and cyclists, crossing the railway lines at Leangen Station as part of Trondheim’s main walking and cycling route towards the city centre.The most unusual feature is its material. The bridge deck uses 100% recycled aluminium recovered from Gyda. The wider structure is made from aluminium, while the tension rods are made from stainless steel. Light Metal Age described the all-aluminium network arch construction with a fully recycled deck as the first of its kind in the world.The choice of aluminium also affected how the bridge could be handled during construction. Hydro reported that its relatively low weight allowed the structure to be assembled away from the railway and later lifted into position. Compared with a steel version, the aluminium bridge weighs about one-third as much, according to Light Metal Age.The bridge was assembled before the final liftThe construction process was planned around a single major lifting operation. The bridge was test-assembled at Leirvik’s facility in Stord in December 2024. Its four main segments were then transported to Trondheim in March 2025, where workers joined them and fitted suspension rods, railings and safety nets.On 19 June 2025, Nordic Crane lifted the fully assembled bridge into position at Leangen Station. The operation used a 650-tonne crawler crane with a 72-metre boom. The separate components had arrived in 21 truckloads before being assembled at the site.The lift had to take place during a scheduled railway closure, giving the construction team a limited window in which to complete the operation. The Norwegian Public Roads Administration said the critical elements aligned as planned and the installation was completed within the designated period.Recycled aluminium for future bridgesThe project is intended to be more than a single crossing. Hangarbrua forms part of the Norwegian Public Roads Administration’s FjordX research and development programme, which focuses on developing infrastructure that is cost-efficient, environmentally sustainable and safe. Sensors installed throughout the bridge will monitor its structural behaviour and provide data for further research.The information gathered could help researchers and engineers understand how aluminium performs when used as a structural material and could contribute to future design standards for aluminium bridges. The bridge has already been used as a research subject by master’s and doctoral students at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology.Leirvik also sees the project as a starting point for exploring aluminium bridges with different designs and spans. The company had extensive experience producing large aluminium structures for the oil and gas industry, but Hangarbrua marked its return to aluminium bridge construction after the Forsmo Bridge, which it delivered in 1995.How much difference can the material choice makeThe environmental case for the bridge was assessed by COWI through a life cycle analysis comparing the aluminium design with a stainless-steel version of the same network arch concept. Light Metal Age reported that the analysis estimated 120 tonnes of CO2 emissions for the aluminium bridge when the benefits of recycling at the end of its life were included, compared with 500 tonnes for the stainless-steel alternative. Without those end-of-life benefits, the figures were 420 tonnes and 620 tonnes respectively.Aluminium’s resistance to corrosion is another part of the design. Hydro said the bridge is expected to need minimal maintenance over its lifetime, while the Norwegian Public Roads Administration reported an expectation of maintenance-free performance for 100 years.

articles.title: Starlink: Why Elon Musk is taking on Mukesh Ambani and Jio over satellite internet
articles.summary: Musk has taken pot-shots at Reliance owner Mukesh Ambani as Starlink struggles to launch in India.
articles.body:
Elon Musk has questioned whether billionaire Mukesh Ambani is the "real boss of India" as his satellite internet company Starlink struggles to secure final approval to launch in the country.

The remark came a day after Musk accused unnamed powerful business interests of trying to block Starlink's entry into India. He then singled out Ambani, whose Reliance conglomerate owns Jio, India's biggest mobile network operator.

India has rejected Musk's allegations, saying its satellite communications rules are fair and non-discriminatory.

Ambani and Reliance Group have not responded to Musk's remarks. The BBC has reached out to them for comment

The row comes as competition grows in India's satellite internet market, with Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel also preparing to launch services.

The rivalry is complicated by the fact that Starlink has also partnered with Ambani's Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel.

In March 2025, both companies signed agreements with SpaceX to distribute Starlink equipment and services in India, subject to government approval. The companies also said they could explore sharing network infrastructure. The BBC has also reached out to Bharti Airtel for comment.

Musk first made the allegations on Wednesday, accusing "certain oligarchs" of maintaining a "monopolistic chokehold" on Indian consumers.

"You can guess who they are," he wrote on X , adding that blocking Starlink was "a crime against the people of India".

On Thursday, India's Ministry of Communications responded, saying that three operators - Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb and Jio Satellite Communications - were at broadly the same stage of the approval process, with all three awaiting security clearances and spectrum allocation before they can launch commercial services.

"The suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived," the ministry said, without naming Musk directly.

Musk continued to question the delay, saying Starlink was already licensed in more than 165 countries.

"Starlink is licensed in over 165 countries and has spent five years complying with every single law and requirement of the government of India, so why still no license? Is Ambani the real boss of India?" he wrote on X on Thursday.

Starlink, owned by Musk's SpaceX, uses satellites in low Earth orbit to provide internet access, particularly in remote areas where mobile networks and broadband cables are difficult or expensive to install.

The company has been trying to enter India since 2021 and has secured key licences. But it still needs final security clearances and spectrum allocation before it can begin commercial services.

Wednesday's row unfolded as senior executives from Starlink, Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel gathered at the India Mobile Congress in Delhi, where all three companies discussed their plans for satellite internet services.

Speaking at the event, Akash Ambani, chairman of Reliance Jio Infocomm and Mukesh Ambani's son, said the company was developing its own satellite communications technology and working towards regulatory approvals.

Asked by a reporter about Musk's allegations, Akash declined to comment and only said, "We want to be heads down and deliver value to our Indian consumers."

Bharti Airtel chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal said his company's satellite venture was also awaiting government approvals.

SpaceX executive Lauren Dreyer, who oversees Starlink's business operations, said the company had spent years working with Indian regulators and had built security controls into its network to meet the country's requirements.

Security has been a key concern surrounding Starlink's entry into India. In 2024, Indian authorities said they had recovered Starlink equipment during a drug-smuggling investigation in the remote Andaman and Nicobar Islands and an army operation in the northeastern state of Manipur.

Musk said at that time that Starlink's service had never been active in India, arguing that the equipment recovered by authorities could not have been using its satellite network.

Questions also remain over how affordable the service would be for Indian consumers, particularly those in rural areas.

India is one of the world's largest internet markets but access remains uneven, particularly in remote areas where mobile networks and broadband cables are difficult or expensive to build.

Musk has argued that Starlink could help bridge this gap. "Starlink in India would enable high-speed, affordable internet connectivity for those who can't afford current prices or who don't have a connection at all!" he wrote on X on Wednesday.

The company has yet to announce prices for India, but some experts say its plans elsewhere suggest the service could be beyond the reach of many Indian households.

In the US, Starlink's residential plans start at $55 a month, although prices and equipment costs vary by plan and location.

articles.title: Nasa struggled to find a safe sampling site on asteroid Bennu; Queen guitarist Brian May used his little-known 3D imaging skills to reveal its treacherous terrain
articles.summary: A rock musician working at a computer might seem an unlikely figure in an asteroid-sampling mission, but Brian May brought a specialist skill to Nasa’s
articles.body: A rock musician working at a computer might seem an unlikely figure in an asteroid-sampling mission, but Brian May brought a specialist skill to Nasa’s search for a place to land on Bennu. The Queen guitarist, who also holds a doctorate in astrophysics, helped scientists turn spacecraft photographs into three-dimensional views of the asteroid’s rough surface. The work became particularly useful when the images revealed a landscape far more crowded with boulders than mission planners had anticipated. May’s contribution, made alongside planetary scientist Claudia Manzoni, later became part of a book documenting Bennu’s unusual terrain and the challenges faced by Nasa’s OSIRIS-REx mission.How Brian May turned spacecraft photographs into 3D viewsMay joined the OSIRIS-REx science team in January 2019, several months after the spacecraft arrived at Bennu. His involvement grew from an existing friendship with Dante Lauretta, the mission’s principal investigator, and a shared interest in astronomy. Lauretta was also a Queen fan, though the guitarist was expected to contribute scientific expertise rather than simply lend his name to the project.May had spent years developing an interest in stereoscopic photography, a technique that allows viewers to perceive depth by combining two images taken from slightly different viewpoints. With the right image pairs, the brain interprets the differences between them as a three-dimensional scene. May had used this approach to produce views of Pluto from Nasa’s New Horizons mission and of Comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko, which was visited by the European Space Agency’s Rosetta spacecraft.OSIRIS-REx did not carry a dedicated stereo camera. That did not prevent May from applying the technique. By identifying suitable photographs captured at different angles and carefully aligning them, he could create three-dimensional representations from images that were originally recorded by a single camera. These views gave the mission team a better sense of the height, depth and relative positions of features scattered across Bennu.Why Nasa struggled to find a suitable landing siteWhen OSIRIS-REx reached the asteroid, scientists had anticipated finding relatively open areas that might accommodate the spacecraft’s sampling manoeuvre. The mission had been designed around the possibility of landing in a comparatively smooth patch of ground.The images told a different story. Bennu, which measures approximately 500 metres in diameter, was covered with rocks and boulders, leaving little of the open terrain that engineers had expected. Some formations rose tens of feet above the surface. From conventional two-dimensional photographs, judging the precise shape of the ground and the distance between obstacles was difficult.May worked through the incoming photographs with Manzoni, searching for image pairs that could reveal the terrain more clearly. The task involved examining numerous craters and assessing whether any contained a sufficiently large, accessible patch of ground. May later recalled that he had spent so much time on the work that his musical activities took a back seat.In the book Bennu 3-D: Anatomy of an Asteroid, Lauretta described how the resulting images helped the team appreciate the difficulty of operating on the asteroid. The three-dimensional views made its uneven surface easier to understand and helped scientists and engineers assess possible sampling locations with greater confidence.Nasa narrowed its search to two potential landing sitesThe search eventually narrowed to two candidates: Osprey and Nightingale. Neither offered the broad, uncomplicated landing area originally envisaged. Osprey measured roughly six metres across, while Nightingale was around eight metres wide, making both considerably smaller than the 25-metre target area in the original mission design.Each site had its advantages. Osprey appealed to the engineering team because there were fewer potentially hazardous rocks around its rim. Nightingale attracted the scientists, who believed its surface material might preserve a useful record of Bennu’s history. The colour and composition of the regolith, the loose material covering the asteroid, made the crater an especially interesting place to collect a sample. The decision meant accepting a difficult approach, with a large boulder near the crater’s edge adding to the hazards. The team had to work out how the spacecraft could descend through the surrounding terrain and reach the sampling point without striking nearby rocks.The sampling attempt revealed another surpriseOSIRIS-REx touched down at Nightingale in October 2020. The spacecraft used its sampling mechanism to contact the surface and collect material before moving away from the asteroid.The operation exposed another mistaken assumption about Bennu. Scientists had expected the surface to behave more like a firm layer of gravel, with some dust and small particles disturbed by contact. Instead, images recorded during the manoeuvre showed a substantial quantity of debris moving around the spacecraft.Bennu’s surface offered far less resistance than expected. The loose collection of rocks, gravel and dust shifted under the probe, raising concerns about how easily the spacecraft might have become trapped or damaged during the operation. The asteroid’s extremely weak gravity also meant that particles and boulders could behave in unfamiliar ways.Bennu is classified as a rubble-pile asteroid, a body made up of fragments held together by gravity rather than a single solid mass of rock. Its structure helps explain why a seemingly straightforward touchdown could produce such an unexpected response. Material that appeared stable from a distance could move when disturbed.A successful return with more material than plannedDespite the difficult terrain and the unexpected behaviour of the surface, OSIRIS-REx completed its main objective. As reported by Space.com, NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft departed asteroid Bennu on 10 May 2021, beginning its journey back to Earth with a sample of rocks and dust that exceeded the mission’s minimum collection target of 60 grams.The sample was returned to Earth in September 2023, when the capsule landed in Utah. Scientists gained material that could be examined directly in laboratories, allowing them to investigate Bennu’s composition and the processes that shaped it. The mission was Nasa’s first to collect a sample from an asteroid and bring it back to Earth.Bennu is of particular interest because material preserved within primitive asteroids can provide evidence about conditions in the early solar system. Its loose structure also matters for planetary defence. Scientists need to understand how an asteroid might respond to an attempted deflection, and the spacecraft’s interaction with Bennu offered useful information about the behaviour of its surface.The asteroid has a small but measurable chance of striking Earth in the coming centuries. Estimates cited by the mission team put the probability of an impact at approximately one in 1,800. That does not make a collision likely, but it gives scientists a reason to study the object carefully.A book documenting Bennu in three dimensionsMay and Lauretta presented Bennu 3-D: Anatomy of an asteroid at London’s Natural History Museum in July 2023. Published with the University of Arizona Press and the London Stereoscopic Company, the illustrated volume brings together photographs and stereoscopic views of the asteroid. It also includes 3D glasses, allowing readers to see the images with a sense of depth.The book records more than the appearance of an unusual space rock. It shows how visual techniques developed outside the usual spacecraft imaging process could help scientists interpret data from a mission facing an unexpected problem.

articles.title: Michael Dell, biggest donor to Trump Accounts, defends change in rules; says: Hard for me to believe that's a bad thing, these children are going to somehow be negatively ...
articles.summary: Michael Dell has come out strongly in defense of updated federal regulations governing Trump Accounts, dismissing warnings from skeptics who claim that
articles.body: Michael Dell has come out strongly in defense of updated federal regulations governing Trump Accounts, dismissing warnings from skeptics who claim that permitting donors to gift individual corporate shares directly into children’s portfolios poses ethical or financial hazards. Speaking this week in an interview with Yahoo Finance, the Dell Technologies founder and billionaire philanthropist rejected allegations that such donations are part of an effort to manipulate young minds or asset markets.“It’s kind of hard for me to believe that’s a bad thing, right?” the tech titan said, adding, “That these children are going to somehow be negatively influenced because they now have one share of SpaceX, but they didn’t have before, right? The alternative is they didn’t have it, right?”“It seems unlikely that that is some kind of devious plot to somehow influence these 2 million children. If anything, they’re going to be interested in space and capitalism and how capital markets work, compounding and investing, and it will spark an interest in them that hopefully helps them as they become adults,” he added.Moving beyond low-cost index fundsTrump Accounts, originally authorised under last year's One Big Beautiful Tax bill, are tax-advantaged savings and investment tools structured to help children build nest eggs for retirement, college education or launching a business. Under the inaugural framework, all account contributions were required by law to sit in low-cost index funds to maximise market diversification.However, rule changes enacted last week permit charitable organisations and donors to place individual company equities into children’s accounts. So far, SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell stands as the only major donor to commit corporate equity under the revised guidelines, promising more than 2 million shares of SpaceX stock to assist lower-income youths aged 11 to 17 living in disadvantaged communities.The policy alteration has drawn sharp criticism from financial analysts and ethicists who caution that directing children’s wealth toward single corporate entities ties their future economic baseline to an isolated business rather than broad, resilient market indices. Moreover, it has been alleged that wealthy donors could potentially orchestrate massive equity contributions to children’s funds as a means to capture tax write-offs or support corporate share prices.Michael Dell’s $6.25 billion pledge and the drive for automatic enrollmentDell and his wife, Susan, represent the single largest private donor block for the program. The couple has committed $6.25 billion to deposit $250 directly into the accounts of 25 million American children. As of October 7, more than 10 million children had received their $250 deposits, totaling $2.6 billion deployed, with the remaining balance of the full $6.25 billion pledge expected to clear by Friday (October 9).Dell noted that private sector participation is picking up speed:“I believe there will be a number of additional philanthropists that join us. We have now many employers that are joining in the fund here and either matching the government's contribution or going much larger and contributing to the accounts of the children that work inside their companies or even children in the communities where they operate their businesses.”The private contributions coincide with a major administrative pivot by the U.S. Department of the Treasury. On October 1, the agency transitioned Trump Accounts from a voluntary setup to automatic enrollment, establishing accounts for nearly 70 million American children under the age of 18 who hold a valid Social Security number.You use AI every day.
